A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OutFormer work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, synthetic-data simulations, curriculum and prior ablations, timing measurements, and per-dataset results with standard deviations over five seeds.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical studies and adds categorical-data evaluations, bin-count and ensemble-size experiments, and GMM goodness-of-fit analyses.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix H introduce categorical-input adaptations: one-hot encoding with feature subsampling, and an alternative XStream projection into 100 numerical features. The underlying Transformer, synthetic priors, SEC algorithm, losses and core inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds an explicitly categorical-heavy and mixed-input evaluation scenario covering six TALENT-derived tasks and IEEE-CIS-Fraud (Appendix H). This extends the represented feature types and task conditions. TALENT was already a data source in v1, but this categorical-feature evaluation is new; the original four benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the retained benchmark and curriculum comparisons is unchanged. The new categorical evaluation reuses IForest, while XStream supplies an input transformation rather than an independently evaluated detector. The revised IForest hyperparameter setting belongs to E3.

E3.justification: Table 13 changes IForest's stated max_features setting from [1, 2] to [1.0], without establishing whether experiments were rerun. New protocols include categorical-feature selection, 15–20% outlier sampling and IForest-based dataset filtering, controlled bin-count sweeps, and ensemble-size evaluations stratified by effective dataset size. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 tests sensitivity to SEC bin count and the latency–accuracy trade-off across ensemble sizes (Appendices G.3.3–G.4). Appendix I adds GMM-fit-conditioned and large/high-dimensional case analyses, largely reusing existing ADBench scores. Appendix H also compares categorical input representations.

E5.justification: Appendix I introduces GMM goodness-of-fit assessment using BIC-selected mixtures, two-sample testing and reported p-values. Existing five-seed standard deviations and permutation/Wilcoxon testing remain unchanged. Changed p-values in retained tables do not establish a change in their statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 4, 16–17 and 22–25 revise numerous results. In Table 4, LOF's rAUC changes from 0.142 to 0.869 and IForest's from 0.143 to 0.883; OutFormer's average rank changes from 4.28 to 5.06, versus DTE-NP's 4.30 to 5.04. v2 also adds categorical, bin-count, ensemble and goodness-of-fit outcomes. These are revised reported comparisons, not established same-setting performance gains; the PDFs do not explain the aggregate revisions.

T1.justification: Appendix G.4 newly defines effective dataset size as S = (#context points × #features)/(5,000 × 100), with corresponding size strata. This is a limited mathematical definition supporting evaluation. The PFN formulation, SEC mathematics and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: zero-shot tabular detection through mixed synthetic priors and SEC, competitive or state-of-the-art performance, and low inference latency. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting excessive bin counts to noisy reward estimates, ensemble benefits to context diversity, and projection weaknesses to lost categorical signals. Appendix I relates gains to poor GMM fit while acknowledging multiple contributing factors. The original limitations in Appendix B are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Hugging Face access pointer, identifies default baseline settings in Table 13, and documents preprocessing and configurations for the new studies. The detailed original architecture, hardware, training schedule and inference implementation remain unchanged. The additional access information is reported in the PDF; its availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting IEEE-CIS-Fraud, XStream preprocessing and goodness-of-fit testing. TALENT was already cited in v1. The extended related-work discussion and positioning relative to FOMO-0D remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The original exposition is largely retained. v2 extends Section 5.2, adds Section 5.3 and appendices covering the new studies, and inserts publication and conflict-of-interest text. These are localized structural additions rather than a broad rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn as a larger three-panel workflow, and Tables 30–36 display the added analyses. The original per-dataset Tables 30–32 become Tables 37–39, while Table 13 adds default-setting emphasis. Most existing figures, table structures and the document's visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful evidence about categorical transfer, SEC sensitivity and ensemble costs that v1 lacked, alongside a clearer framework diagram and additional reproducibility information. These improve understanding of practical behavior. The gains are limited by unexplained aggregate-result revisions and imperfect reporting: the categorical text claims five wins over IForest, while Table 34 displays four strict wins and one tie. The additions support a modest overall improvement rather than a substantial resolution of the paper's evidential limitations.
